newsitem.title: INDIA: India protests against U.S. export controls.
newsitem.headline: India protests against U.S. export controls.

text.p: India has protested to the United States against export controls on two Indian firms and two research centres that Washington believes could spur arms proliferation, a government minister has said.
"The government has taken up this matter with the U.S. authorities," Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah said.

"India's opposition to such ad hoc discriminatory export control regimes has been reiterated to the U.S. government," the minister said in a written reply to a parliamentarian's question released on Tuesday.

In February, the U.S. Commerce Department began imposing restrictions on entities it believed could contribute to weapons of mass destruction. The restrictions stemmed from a U.S. law aimed at checking nuclear non-proliferation.
Israel's Ben-Gurion University was the first to be named, and it was followed in May by India's state-run Bharat Electronics Ltd.
Indian Rare Earths Ltd, the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre and the Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research were named in June.
U.S. exporters will have to apply for licences from authorities in Washington to sell goods to companies or institutions on the list, even if the products they want to sell are not controlled.

Ramaiah said New Delhi had told Washington that its past record demonstrated that sensitive items imported by Indian institutions would not be re-exported to countries where they could be put to military use.
"India's exemplary record in not permitting export of these items to countries where it could be used for non-civilian purposes has been pointed out," the minister said.

India successfully conducted an underground atomic test in 1974, but says it does possess nuclear weapons. U.S. officials believe both India and neighbouring Pakistan could quickly assemble nuclear weapons.
New Delhi says it will use nuclear energy only for peaceful purposes, and pursues an active programme to generate power from nuclear reactors.
